transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
This is the final week of the midterm campaign season.
The latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll sheds light on the issues driving voters across
the ideological spectrum.
Cost of living, top of mind overall, with a third of respondents saying they've experienced
hardship in the past year.
The preservation of democracy continues to resonate with Democrats and independents
while immigration is the biggest concern for self-described MAGA supporters.
NPR's Hunzi Lo Wang reports more than 32 million ballots have already been cast during
early voting in the midterms.
Voters have returned more than 16 million mail-in ballots around the country.
They've also gassed more than 16 million ballots in person at early voting sites.
That's according to statistics compiled by the University of Florida's election lab.
More voters are set to exercise their rights at the polls before next Tuesday's election
day.
Early in-person voting starts tomorrow in Oklahoma and on Thursday in Kentucky.
For mail-in voters, today is the U.S. Postal Service's recommended deadline for mailing
back ballots in states where they must be received by election day.
Voters can also consider returning their mail-in ballot at their local election office or
at any available ballot drop box.
And if you're eligible to vote in North Carolina's midterm elections but haven't registered
yet, your last chance is at early voting sites this Saturday, Halloween.
Hunzi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Israeli voters are deciding whether to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
He's got supporters like Itamar Ariel.
The best.
And Erran Nitzan, drumming outside a polling station in a suburb of Tel Aviv, also a supporter.
But NPR's Daniel Estrin says Netanyahu also faces heavy opposition following the last
three years of war.
The election official says it's the highest recorded voter turnout in more than 50 years.
It reflects the attitude of many in the country about the importance of this election.
Voter Naama Aronson.
Important is an underestimation because it's much more than important.
It's crucial.
I'm worried, really worried of what's going to become of our country if there's not a major
change.
There's high enthusiasm among voters seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu,
while some of Netanyahu's former supporters have said they won't vote for him now after
he failed to prevent the October 7th Hamas attacks.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Vatican says Pope Leo XIV plans to meet with survivors of clergy sexual abuse when
he travels to Latin America next month.
Its statement today says the pontiff is scheduled to hold several meetings as he seeks to express
"solidarity with those who have suffered and continue to suffer as a result of this violence."
There were questions about whether the trip would even happen after his surgery this month
for lung cancer.
He scheduled stops in Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru.
It's NPR.
President Trump returns to Texas today with Republicans facing the prospect of losing
congressional races that were previously projected to be easy wins.
Trump has again raised concerns about voter fraud as he's done in previous election cycles.
He has offered a $1 million reward for tips on fraud.
The number of American kids with their own smartphones doubles between the ages of nine
and ten, according to a new survey by the online advocacy group Common Sense Media.
NPR's Rita Chatterjee reports a significant number of tweens are using social media and
AI platforms that are intended only for adolescents age 13 and up.
In a survey of more than a thousand tweens and teens across the country, more than half
of 11-year-olds had their own smartphones, as did 97% of 17-year-olds.
Nearly half of tweens use social media for at least an hour and a half each day and a
similar number use AI chatbots.
That's despite the minimum age for both kinds of platforms being 13 years.
Tweens and teens are spending an increasing amount of time on screens outside of school
and homework, tweens spend roughly five hours a day on digital media for entertainment,
where teens spend about eight hours a day.
AI chatbots and short videos on TikTok and YouTube are taking up a significant chunk
of their time.
Rita Chatterjee, NPR News.
The South African company TransNet is claiming the record for operating the longest-ever
freight train, a 4.7-mile train powered by electric and diesel locomotives on a test
run earlier this month that says it traveled 534 miles.
It's NPR News.

topics.text: Final week of midterm campaign season, with the NPR/PBS/Marist poll on voter concerns
Over 32 million midterm ballots already cast in early voting, per University of Florida election lab
Early voting begins in Oklahoma and Kentucky; mail ballot deadlines and North Carolina registration reminder
Israeli voters go to polls in election that could oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with record turnout
Vatican says Pope Leo XIV will meet clergy sexual abuse survivors on Latin America trip next month
President Trump returns to Texas as Republicans face losing previously safe congressional races; renews voter fraud claims
Common Sense Media survey finds smartphone ownership doubles between ages nine and ten among American kids
South African company TransNet claims record for longest freight train, a 4.7-mile test run
